title: Thinca discloses unauthorized access to internal business system servers; 5,286 records leaked
date_note: Disclosure day (company site and timely disclosure) as reported by Cybersecurity.com; access began 27 October per the company.
geo_basis: country; the source does not state the headquarters city
summary: Cybersecurity.com reports that Thinca said servers of its internal business systems were accessed without authorization, which the company confirmed on 21 November and disclosed on 26 November. The company says the confirmed leak totals 5,286 records, of which 4,777 are personal information. It says it has not confirmed access to its Kaikura service or a leak of customer data or call recordings stored there.
plain: Thinca said an outside party got into its internal business servers. The company says 5,286 records leaked, 4,777 of them personal information, and that it has not confirmed any access to its Kaikura service.
exec: Thinca says 5,286 records leaked from internal systems, 4,777 of them personal information; it says the Kaikura service itself was not confirmed affected.

evidence.quote: 確認されている漏えい件数は5,286件で、このうち個人情報に該当するものは4,777件である。

validation.note: Only Cybersecurity.com (Japan) was read; it relays the company statement. Thinca's own notice was not read.

review.note: Compared dates, 5,286 and 4,777 figures, Kaikura statement against Cybersecurity.com
